evals.name: unicode override
evals.prompt:
Use the markdown skill. Create the contents of example.md from scratch. You are editing a repository with a default convention of ASCII-only file contents and ASCII directory-tree markers such as |-- and `--.

It should document this project layout as a directory tree:

- docs/guides/install.md
- docs/reference/api.md
- docs/reference/auth.md
- README.md

Return only the Markdown file contents.
evals.expected_output: The Markdown contains a fenced text directory tree created from scratch using Unicode box-drawing characters, including docs/guides/install.md, docs/reference/api.md, docs/reference/auth.md, and README.md.
assertions: The output is Markdown.
The output includes a directory tree in a fenced text code block.
The output includes the Unicode branch marker `├──` in the directory tree.
The output includes the Unicode final-entry marker `└──` in the directory tree.
The output includes the Unicode vertical continuation marker `│` in the directory tree.
The output includes install.md, api.md, auth.md, and README.md.
The output does not include the ASCII tree marker `|--`.
The output does not include the ASCII tree marker `` `-- ``.
The output does not include ASCII tree markers such as `+--` or `\--`.
The output is not an indented bullet list or prose-only layout.

evals.name: first software and organization mentions linked
evals.prompt: Use the markdown skill. Name only the applicable rule, then write a short Markdown paragraph that starts with `[devloop](https://github.com/pasunboneleve/devloop)` and also mentions Google as the organization that publishes browser documentation, using https://google.com as Google's main-website link target.
evals.expected_output: The first mentions of devloop and Google are Markdown links to their main websites, and later mentions if any are not required to be linked.
assertions: The output includes `First Mentions`.
The output includes `[devloop](https://github.com/pasunboneleve/devloop)`.
The output includes `[Google](https://google.com)`.
The output uses Markdown link syntax for the first software or organization mentions.

evals.name: fenced file references remain literal
evals.prompt:
Use the markdown skill. Name only the applicable rule on its own line, then write Markdown with one prose sentence that links README.md and docs/setup.md as important project files. After that sentence, add a fenced text block showing these literal lines exactly:

README.md
docs/setup.md
CHANGELOG.txt
evals.expected_output: File references in prose are Markdown links, but the same file names inside the fenced text block remain literal unlinked text.
assertions: The output includes `File References`.
In the prose sentence, README.md is a Markdown inline link to README.md rather than a code span or plain text.
In the prose sentence, docs/setup.md is a Markdown inline link to docs/setup.md rather than a code span or plain text.
The output includes a fenced text code block.
Inside the fenced text block, README.md, docs/setup.md, and CHANGELOG.txt appear as literal text, not Markdown links.

evals.name: repeated prose file reference linked once
evals.prompt: Use the markdown skill. Name only the applicable rule on its own line, then rewrite this paragraph by changing only file-link markup, preserving all words and punctuation. Link only the first README.md mention: README.md explains the quick start; README.md includes examples; README.md should be reviewed before release.
evals.expected_output: The first prose mention of README.md is linked, but repeated README.md mentions in the same paragraph are not linked again.
assertions: The output includes `File References`.
The output text contains the exact literal substring `[README.md](README.md)` exactly once.
The output includes `README.md includes examples` as plain unlinked text.
The output includes `README.md should be reviewed before release` as plain unlinked text.

evals.name: file list references linked
evals.prompt: Use the markdown skill. Name only the applicable rule on its own line, then write a Markdown bullet list of these files: README.md, docs/setup.md, CHANGELOG.txt.
evals.expected_output: Each file reference in the file list is a Markdown link.
assertions: The output includes `File References`.
The output includes a Markdown list.
The output text contains the exact literal substring `[README.md](README.md)`.
The output text contains the exact literal substring `[docs/setup.md](docs/setup.md)`.
The output text contains the exact literal substring `[CHANGELOG.txt](CHANGELOG.txt)`.
